_comment: Ids from owed-baseline.txt that the CURRENT golden no longer owes (moved to SKIP/FAIL, or
dropped from cells.json) — named here with an owner and a rationale so the loss is a decision,
not silence. replay.sh reads this file; an id it does not cover is RED. `cells` is a regex over
the cell id (same convention as accepted-differences.json's `cells` field).
Coverage GROWING (a new id owed that was not in the baseline) needs no entry here — it is
always allowed and just printed; only a SHRINK needs to be named.
Nothing has been dropped from the 1.5.5 golden since owed-baseline.txt was generated from
golden/1.5.5/ledger.tsv's PASS rows. The entries below are cells that have NEVER been owed:
each is a `needs_fixture` SKIP that carries an accepted-differences.json entry naming a
deliberate 1.6.0 improvement over 1.5.5, so recording it would produce a divergence the
improvement register cannot forgive without an owner decision (a usage/status class ->
kind=breaking) OR needs a capability the oracle may not build for itself (a pinned-mock verb,
a concurrent-window-roll driver). They are named here so the reason each is not recorded is
written down and owned, and so the entry is already in place the day the cell is baselined and
then re-loses its fixture. Two of the five dormant accepted-differences ids reviewed alongside
these carry NO cell to name and stay documented solely in accepted-differences.json: PR2-D5
(route.failover|fb|member-slow does not exist -- closing it needs a fallback-pool member
override in oracle-config.sh, a new cell, and a fresh 1.5.5 recording) and S-14 (no gemini
speech/TTS cell exists -- every llm cell is op=chat, and a speech leaf needs a fixture, a
pinned-mock speech verb, and the product's refusal-envelope decision).
TODO item 51 added the entries from `boot-refusal-needs-a-feature-off-binary` onward: every OTHER
in-scope cell (any cell outside the mcp/a2a conformance-rig families) that the committed golden
does not owe, each with the reason it has no golden reference. They carry no accepted-differences
twin. scripts/verify-1.6.0-done.sh (assert_golden_bookkeeping, run by its --selftest over this
tree) refuses an in-scope cell the golden does not owe and no entry here names.

The three entries from `admin-kernel-verbs-new-in-1.6.0` onward name the 89 admin.ops cells the admin corpus gained when it was reconciled against the served router: operations 1.5.5 never had, so the 1.5.5 golden cannot owe them. Each regex enumerates its operations; none is a family blanket.

2026-10-14 (owner rule 22; busbar-release #369 and #372; coordinator ruling 2026-10-14, conformance-gaps D): stream-upstream-error, gemini-tool-use-token-term, bedrock-cachepoint-before-document and responses-url-citation are retired: the recorder records those nine cells as new `<old id>@fixture` ids (the bare ids' SKIP rows are retired whole in golden/1.5.5/retired.tsv), owed-baseline.txt owes them and their 1.5.5 goldens are committed (oracle-rerecord, add-only).

accepted.rationale: BOOT-059a and BOOT-079 fire only on a binary built WITHOUT `hooks-ranking`, BOOT-094 only on one built WITHOUT `auth-admin-tokens` (fixtures/boot-mutations.json notes). The published 1.5.5 binary carries both features, so the branch is unreachable in the only binary the golden may be taken from; no config, env or argument can reach it. It is not recorded because the committed 1.5.5 golden (testing/shadow-oracle/golden/1.5.5, meta.json at 2026-09-16) scored it a needs_fixture SKIP, and giving it a golden reference means re-taking that recording from the published 1.5.5 binary, which only the owner's golden re-take (TODO item 50, the oracle-rerecord workflow) may do; an agent may not bless or re-record a golden (TODO rule 9.2). Named here (TODO item 51) so the missing reference is an owned decision rather than a SKIP nobody wrote a reason for.

From config.yaml both refusals are pre-empted by an earlier stage: an inline `auth.chain` map entry or `chain: [tokens]` trips the legacy-config detector (BOOT-P41) before deserialization, and a `token:` on a named definition trips BOOT-074c first (fixtures/boot-mutations.json notes). Reaching them needs an admin-API/overlay fixture the recorder does not have. It is not recorded because the committed 1.5.5 golden (testing/shadow-oracle/golden/1.5.5, meta.json at 2026-09-16) scored it a needs_fixture SKIP, and giving it a golden reference means re-taking that recording from the published 1.5.5 binary, which only the owner's golden re-take (TODO item 50, the oracle-rerecord workflow) may do; an agent may not bless or re-record a golden (TODO rule 9.2). Named here (TODO item 51) so the missing reference is an owned decision rather than a SKIP nobody wrote a reason for.

The 57 admin.ops cells (ok + unauth for each of the 28 operations the node's administrative kernel loop serves, plus PostStoreRestore's bad-body) that the admin corpus gained when it was reconciled against the served router (items 44/45/46). It is not recorded because the committed 1.5.5 golden (testing/shadow-oracle/golden/1.5.5, meta.json at 2026-09-16) was taken before the cell existed and the published 1.5.5 binary has no such operation: its served document (admin.ops|GetOpenapiJson|ok, 49 paths) names none of these paths, so a 1.5.5 recording could only capture the router's unmatched-path 404. This is NEW 1.6.0 surface, not a difference from 1.5.5, so no accepted-differences.json twin exists or is owed; the cell is judged by its own contract (the served-surface reconciliation test, crates/busbar-core-admin/src/v1/json/tests/served_surface.rs) until the 1.6.0 golden is cut.

no 1.5.5 baseline; predev fence. 1.5.5 had no a2a or mcp plane, so golden/1.5.5 cannot owe what busbar sends their upstreams. These cells are owed instead by testing/shadow-oracle/fence/predev-275cbd80b/ (recorded twice, byte-identical, from a clean release build of predev 275cbd80b; ARCHITECT ruling 2026-09-28), which bin/oracle replay judges in its own 'predev fence' section. They are never merged into golden/1.5.5, and they are re-recorded only under an ARCHITECT ruling.

no 1.5.5 baseline; predev fence. 1.5.5 had no decisions plane, so no 1.5.5 cell can owe one. Since FLIP-DECISIONS the plane is served through its door (the `plane-decisions` row, busbar_plane_decisions::plane_door): POST /v1/systemone for exactly one configured decisions model, a keyed data-plane caller, the caller's body and the far end's answer relayed byte for byte, one request fee and the reported decision units ledgered on a success. Those served bytes are proven by the jev conformance suite (the jev suite, conformance/registry.toml) and crates/busbar/src/root/tests/serve_tests.rs. The fence for its metering and egress is recorded from a named predev build carrying the flip, into fence/predev-<sha>/ under the same ARCHITECT rules; until it is, no decisions| cell exists, and this entry names that on purpose.

the streams family is a 1.6.0 plane: 1.5.5 never served it, so the 1.5.5 golden holds no reference for these cells and owed-baseline.txt never listed them. Their reference is golden/1.6.0-pre/, recorded from the pinned pre-fold predev build, and the cells carry no 1.5.5 claim.
